- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:921-924, 940 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Four `--repo=upstream` parameterized cases expect a block (`code == 2`) although the documented behavior for an unverified destination is to request confirmation and return code 0.
  WHY: The guard emits `permissionDecision: ask`, so these stale assertions fail in CI; the reviewers identify this as a test expectation defect.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:555-560 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_push_targets` treats the `--repo` value as the destination when a positional repository is also supplied, rather than giving the positional repository precedence.
  WHY: This can misidentify a push to `origin` as targeting an unverified remote and request confirmation instead of checking whether the branch is merged.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:555-560 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The template `_push_targets` has the same positional-repository precedence defect as the live hook.
  WHY: Consumer sessions can misidentify a push to `origin` as targeting an unverified remote and fail to check whether the branch is merged.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:530-537, 1413-1417 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: With `--repo=upstream` and a positional remote such as `origin`, the parser treats `upstream` as the destination and `origin` as a refspec, routing the push to the unverified-destination confirmation path.
  WHY: The four parameterized cases then return code 0 with `permissionDecision: ask` instead of code 2; this review also states the test assertions are stale and the ask behavior is intentional.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:530-537 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The template parser has the same `--repo` and positional-remote behavior as the live hook.
  WHY: The review says the same four CI cases fail through the template copy.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:266, 270, 281, 292-294 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `redirect_fd` is assigned and computed but never read in the live hook.
  WHY: The unused state causes redundant regex work during shell-token parsing without affecting runtime behavior.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:266, 270, 281, 292-294 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `redirect_fd` is assigned and computed but never read in the template hook.
  WHY: The unused state causes redundant regex work during shell-token parsing without affecting runtime behavior.

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR CI must pass on the autofix head SHA (7c0a56d). The PR's own design (agents.md "Merged-PR guard" section, lines 623-640) documents that pushes to an explicit `--repo` or positional remote naming a different or unverified destination request human confirmation, not a block. The PR description's "Proactive fixes included" subsection states: "Pushes with per-command Git configuration... also ask: an override can redirect origin, so the guard does not use its stored PR history to authorize those pushes."
  Expected change site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:916-941 — the `test_push_parser_guards_real_destination` parametrize list. The four cases at lines 921-924 (`git push --repo=upstream origin`, `git push origin --repo=upstream`, `git push origin HEAD:feature/x --repo=upstream`, `git push --repo=upstream origin HEAD:feature/x`) contradict the documented design. They should be removed from this test or moved to a separate "ask" test, with assertions matching `test_push_to_unverified_repository_requires_confirmation`.
  Evidence of absence: pr_check_runs_context.txt shows `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` failing on commit 7c0a56d with four `assert 0 == 2` AssertionError failures on the `--repo=upstream` parametrize cases. The captured stdout on each confirms the guard correctly emits `"permissionDecision": "ask"` (the design intent), but the test demands `code == 2`. The new test cases added by the last run at lines 91-95 and 948-949 cover the leading-redirection-after-assignment feature, not the `--repo=upstream` cases. The same test file also imports a fully correct contract test (`test_push_to_unverified_repository_requires_confirmation`, line 1015) that proves the design is ASK-not-BLOCK for unverified remotes, so the four failing cases are duplicates with the wrong expected value.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
